hypothesis: The v2 basket's losses on 2024-09-01..2026-11-04 are driven by its book mechanics more than by its selection: stops inside normal daily noise exit 67-75% of trades at the stop (9 of 44 on the entry day in 2026), and a 20-session rebalance then leaves the freed capital idle, so the book averages 80-85% cash earning nothing. Widening the stop beyond two daily price bands, refilling the book every 5 sessions and crediting idle cash at the policy rate should raise total return in BOTH windows relative to the unchanged v2 book.

values_chosen_how: A priori, from the diagnosis above and from risk_engine's own geometry (_score_stop already calls a stop inside one band 'triggered by ordinary noise'). No grid, no second value tried. If a run is repeated with other values, that is a new experiment and is recorded as one.

evaluation.baseline: v2 at the parent commit, already measured 2026-11-05 with idle cash uncredited: -0.86% and -9.37% total return. Because E26 also credits cash, the baseline is re-run with the cash credit on and the old stop/cadence, so the stop+cadence effect is read against that, not against the uncredited figure.
evaluation.engine: backtesting/engine.run(engine='v2'), same costs (1.039% round trip), same T+1 and queue model
evaluation.selection_test: examples/basket_random_null.py, 500 draws, seed 20261105, both with the engine's exits and with a fixed 20-session hold
evaluation.also_reported: TEDPIX, equal-weight index, bank deposit, cash share, exit reasons

decision_rule: KEEP the stop and cadence changes as the shipped defaults only if E26 total return exceeds the baseline in BOTH windows. Otherwise set V2_STOP_ATR_MULTIPLE, V2_MIN_STOP_PCT and V2_REBALANCE_SESSIONS back to 2.0, 3% and 20. The idle-cash credit and the panel's fixed-income note are kept either way: they correct a measurement and an omission in the advice, not the strategy.
declared_limits: Both windows were spent on 2026-11-05 by the baseline measurement that motivated this experiment, so E26 CAN show the package is worse and CANNOT establish an edge: an improvement here is an in-sample finding. Beating the baseline is not beating the index, and the decision rule does not claim it is. Any claim of profitability needs sessions after 2026-11-05. The universe is today's listings (survivorship), which flatters every arm equally.
expected_failure: wider stops make losses per stopped trade larger and positions smaller (risk-based sizing), so the book stays mostly in cash and the gain is mostly the cash credit
weekly refills raise turnover and the 1.039% round trip eats the extra exposure

found from a unit test before any run, not from results: a 6% stop puts target 1 (2.5R) 15% away, so overhead resistance that used to trim it to an acceptable reward:risk now drops it below MIN_RISK_REWARD and the BUY becomes AVOID -- fewer buys, more cash
the selection is at or below random (2nd and 20th percentile at baseline); no exit rule can fix that, so the package still trails the index by a wide margin
